---
title: "Install the development preview"
subtitle: "Download a checked binary. No Rust compiler or administrator access needed."
---

::: {.callout-warning}
## Try it on a disposable project
Use sample data or a disposable copy of your project. Production builds
(`proj build`) can modify or remove files, and safety fixes are still pending.
**Never run production builds on the only copy of important work.**
Previews are not a security sandbox; code you run can still change files.
:::

## Choose the preview explicitly

The published [v0.4.0-preview.1](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/releases/tag/v0.4.0-preview.1)
is an early development release. These instructions pin that version.
GitHub's stable **Latest** release is still v0.3.0; it does not contain the
current preview features or the new binary-delivery metadata.

| Download | Requirements |
|---|---|
| Linux / WSL Ubuntu | x86-64 processor, glibc 2.35 or newer; Bash, `curl` and `sha256sum` or `shasum`. Ubuntu 22.04 or newer meets the glibc requirement; user-local installation was verified in WSL Ubuntu 24.04. |
| Windows | x86-64 processor; use PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) for the installer below. |
| macOS / ARM | No binaries supplied for this preview. |

You do not need Git, Rust, Cargo or administrator access to install these binaries.
The [Python tutorial](tutorial.qmd) additionally needs Python 3. Other analysis
tools are needed only if your own scripts or reports use them.

## Ubuntu and WSL Ubuntu

Run this **inside Ubuntu**, not in a Windows terminal. Check that `uname -m`
reports `x86_64` and `getconf GNU_LIBC_VERSION` reports glibc 2.35 or newer.

```bash
mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
installer="$(mktemp)"
curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/bbd12edc8de9865a96b6145d0c7702f1300cb1a8/install-local.sh" -o "$installer" &&
  PROJ_RELEASE_VERSION=0.4.0-preview.1 \
  PROJ_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin" bash "$installer"
rm -f "$installer"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
hash -r
proj --version
```

Expected version: `proj 0.4.0-preview.1`.

The script comes from the reviewed source commit. It downloads the pinned Linux
binary, checks its SHA256 against the release manifest, and installs it as
`~/.local/bin/proj`. It replaces an existing `proj` in that folder only after
verification succeeds. No `sudo` or local compilation is involved.

## Windows

Open **PowerShell 7** (`pwsh`) as your normal user:

```powershell
$installDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".local\bin"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $installDir | Out-Null
$installer = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ("proj-install-" + [guid]::NewGuid() + ".ps1")
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/bbd12edc8de9865a96b6145d0c7702f1300cb1a8/install.ps1" -OutFile $installer
$env:PROJ_RELEASE_VERSION = "0.4.0-preview.1"
$env:PROJ_INSTALL_DIR = $installDir
& $installer
Remove-Item -LiteralPath $installer
$env:Path = "$installDir;$env:Path"
proj --version
```

Expected version: `proj 0.4.0-preview.1`.

The script checks the Windows binary's SHA256 before installing
`proj.exe` in `$HOME\.local\bin`. It does not change system settings or require
an administrator terminal. This installer is checked with PowerShell 7;
these instructions do not claim Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatibility.

## Finding the command later

The PATH lines above make the command available in the **current terminal**.
In a new terminal, repeat that PATH line or add the installation folder to your
own user PATH. The installer does not make that permanent change for you.

Another program can also be named `proj`. Check `command -v proj` in Ubuntu
or `Get-Command proj` in PowerShell, then `proj --version`, if you see unexpected
help or results.

## What the checksum proves

The installer requires the release's `version.txt` and exactly one matching
entry in [checksums.txt](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/releases/download/v0.4.0-preview.1/checksums.txt).
A missing or incorrect checksum stops installation before the existing binary is
replaced. For a manual download, use `sha256sum` on Linux or `Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256`
in PowerShell and compare the result with the manifest's exact filename entry
before running it.

The manifest comes from the same GitHub release. Checksums detect corruption and
mismatches; they are not independent signatures or proof of a reproducible build.
The release also includes
[source-commit.txt](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/releases/download/v0.4.0-preview.1/source-commit.txt)
and [version.txt](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/releases/download/v0.4.0-preview.1/version.txt).
The reviewed source is `bbd12edc8de9865a96b6145d0c7702f1300cb1a8`.

## Start small

Follow [Run your first analysis](tutorial.qmd) with sample data. Broad M1/M2
milestones, R/IDE parity, complete input/code/dependency provenance, and reliable
analysis-free publication retries remain unfinished. Preview recovery is bounded:
it does not isolate every write or undo arbitrary external effects.

See [what works](features.qmd), [detailed preview status](preview-status.qmd) and
[verified delivery notes](release-delivery.qmd) for the evidence and limits.
